findings.evidence: Line 122 LHS scales both arguments. The homogeneity version is true by the same `integral_const_mul` used in the proof at line 123 (`∫ a, r * f a = r * ∫ a, f a` holds unconditionally in Mathlib), so the two statements genuinely compete for the name.
findings.fix: Rename to `densityWeightedPathLength_smul_mul` (arguments named in order: `c • ρ`, `c * ρ₀`), leaving `densityWeightedPathLength_smul` free for the homogeneity statement.
findings.issue: `densityWeightedPathLength_smul` states `densityWeightedPathLength (c • ρ) (c * ρ₀) x v = densityWeightedPathLength ρ ρ₀ x v`, but the name mentions only the `smul` on the first argument; the unconditional homogeneity lemma `densityWeightedPathLength (c • ρ) ρ₀ x v = c * densityWeightedPathLength ρ ρ₀ x v` is what a reader will expect under this name, and it is now blocked.

findings.evidence: Naming conventions: "the name of theorem simply describes the conclusion"; Mathlib names bounds after their RHS, e.g. `Mathlib/Algebra/AlgebraicCard.lean:89 theorem cardinalMk_le_mul`.
findings.fix: Rename to name the right-hand side, e.g. `densityWeightedPathLength_le_mul_geometricPathLength`, and update the module docstring entry at line 46.
findings.issue: `densityWeightedPathLength_le` has a bare `_le`: the name does not say what the bound is (`M / ρ₀ * geometricPathLength S x v`), while the adjacent bound lemma `geometricPathLength_le_diam` (line 143) does name its right-hand side. Other upper bounds for this functional (e.g. by `M / ρ₀ * diam S`) would have no distinguishing name left.

summary: Terminology and namespace are correct and match the roadmap, but two theorem names misdescribe their conclusions: `densityWeightedPathLength_smul` names only one of the two rescaled arguments (and occupies the name of a different, true homogeneity lemma), and `densityWeightedPathLength_le` leaves its bound unnamed, unlike `geometricPathLength_le_diam` next to it.
